newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs fall, index ends at 37-mth closing low.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs fall, index ends at 37-mth closing low.

text.p: Stocks fell across the board with the composite index ending Saturday's half-day session at the lowest level in 37 months, the Korea Stock Exchange said.
Brokers said the overhang of huge margin loans and fears of share oversupply continued to depress the sentiment.
The composite index ended at 730.82, down 8.29 points or 1.12 percent.
The exchange said the index was at its lowest since October 12, 1993, when it closed at 723.57.
Decliners overwhelmed advancers by 793 to 105 while 101 stocks traded unchanged.

"Margin loans continue outpacing customer deposits, and economic prospects are still gloomy. There is no other way for the market to go at such a situation," said Yoo Nam-gil, a researcher at Hyundai Securities.
Loans investors owed to brokerage houses for margin trading stood at 2.88 trillion won, compared with customer deposits at the brokerages of 2.64 trillion, brokers said.
LG Semicon Co, which listed shares on the stock market for the first time, closed at its lower daily limit of 30,800 won after falling 1,900 won.

Brokers said prevailing fears over the semiconductor stocks' gloomy prospects caused massive selling of the shares. The subscription price for the shares was 20,000 won per share during the initial public offering in September.
Despite the overall declines, blue chips closed firmer on bargain hunting. Samsung Electronics ended 2,100 won higher at 65,000 and Hyundai Motor gained 600 won to close at 25,200.
